title: Row-labelled normalized table export
software_contract: export_table(request) fully validates input before materialization, even for copies=0. Invalid input raises ValueError (message unspecified); do not mutate input. Divide each integer entry by the sum of absolute entries in its source row, using Python integer true division to float. All-zero rows become all 0.0; empty rows are also zero rows. Emit copies entries per source row, source-row-major and then copy-index order (indices 0 through copies-1). Return columns (fresh list), source_row_count, export_row_count, zero_row_ids (source order, once per zero source row even for zero copies), column_totals (Python sum in emitted row order for each column; empty totals are integer zero) and entries. Each entry has row_id, copy_index and values (float list). All emitted values lists must be distinct objects and share no mutable list with the request; changing one copy must not change another. Entire output is materialized; no sampling, aggregate-only or lazy substitute is permitted. Empty columns, rows, and zero copies are supported. CLI reads one JSON request and prints one report; invalid input has nonzero exit and no successful report. Python object identity obligations apply to the callable interface; JSON conveys the values and order only.
input_domain: Object with exactly columns (finite list of distinct nonempty strings), rows (finite list), copies (nonnegative Python int, not bool). Each row has exactly row_id (unique nonempty string) and values (finite list of Python integers, not bool, of the same length as columns). Signed integers are valid; floating-point and missing entries are invalid. No artificial row, integer or copy-count cap; sufficient ordinary host memory is assumed for a successful call.
execution_assumptions: The caller consumes every emitted entry and may edit copies independently. Outputs are ordinary classical lists; no external writes or asynchronous operations occur.
No workload distribution, specialized hardware, measured runtime budget or benefit evidence is supplied.
